project.name: Project Beta — Thinking Environment Platform
project.description: A personal operating system that turns messy stream-of-consciousness input into structured projects, tasks, and connected context. Positioned as a thinking environment for people making complex things, not as a task manager and not as an AI wrapper. Built and operated by a single founder.
project.now: 84 open tasks, 8 overdue. Next milestone: 10 daily active users by 2026-09-30.
non_goals: Another task manager — not competing on features with mainstream todo apps. The differentiator is how context is connected, not how todos are listed.
AI wrapper — not positioning as 'AI that does your work'. The moat is the structure and the thinking environment, not agent automation.
Consumption app — not built for passive scrolling. It is for people who make things.
ADHD-only positioning — the ADHD angle is real and resonant but too narrowing as the primary category.
constraints: One-person team. Bandwidth, not ideas, is the binding constraint.
No paid acquisition budget; organic and outreach only.
Founder is simultaneously running a job search, so platform work is on a maintenance ration.

economics.pricing: $20 per user per month, freemium with a 14-day trial

plans.name: 30-Day User Launch Campaign
plans.summary: Drive signups by making one market association obvious: this is a thinking environment that turns messy thinking into structured work. Primary audiences are authors and video creators — the most legible workflows and the easiest before/after demos. Channels: one professional network, one short-form text platform, one visual platform, same thesis adapted per platform. Priority when time is tight: hero proof asset first, then text posts, then visual. Tone leads with relief, not hype; demonstration, not abstraction. Open questions remain on weekly themes, the first hero asset, and signup attribution.

plans.name: Creator Outreach & Content Flywheel
plans.summary: Value-first outreach to 10-15 target creators, executing against the top 3-5. Deliver workflow teardowns rather than product pitches. Success criteria: 3+ partnerships in 60 days, 10+ distributed pieces, measurable signup attribution, and a documented repeatable process. Named risk: one-person bandwidth limits outreach volume; mitigation is quality over quantity.

documents.title: START HERE — Project Beta
documents.content:
## What this is

A personal operating system that minimizes cognitive load by structuring information effectively.

**Core promise:** relief from the cognitive overhead of managing your own work.
**Strategic enemy:** fragmented context and the tools that create it.

## Current state

Primary goal: 10+ daily active users by 2026-09-30. 84 open tasks, 8 overdue.

**Next step:** record the demo video for the reactivation emails. It is the final piece blocking that campaign.

## Standing decisions

- Lead with the thinking-environment category, not with AI.
- ADHD is a supporting wedge, never the headline.
- One-person team: prefer things that compound over things that need staffing.

documents.title: Brand Guide
documents.content: Category: thinking environment for people making complex things. Promise: turn messy thinking into structured work. Differentiator: the project remembers. Moat: context compounds over time. Strategic enemies: tool sprawl, stateless chat, blank-page chaos, productivity theater. Voice: humble but direct; lead with relief rather than hype, demonstration rather than abstraction, replacement rather than addition. Explicitly anti-AI-leading in all public copy.

documents.title: Marketing Strategy
documents.content: Operating strategy for a one-person marketing function. Primary audiences are authors and video creators — the most legible workflows, the easiest before/after demonstrations, and the strongest emotional pain around losing threads of work. Secondary: podcasters, newsletter operators, course creators. Guidance covers what not to spend time on as much as what to do.

documents.title: Guerrilla Content Doctrine
documents.content: Operating doctrine for one-person marketing: what story to tell, what not to tell, and how to publish consistently without a team. Assumes no budget and no staff; every recommended motion must survive a week where the founder has three hours total.

documents.title: Target Audience & Business Model
documents.content: Ideal early users: people managing complex self-directed work, writers, product people. Pain points: rebuilding context repeatedly, disorganization across tools, re-explaining the same background to AI assistants. Pricing: $20 per user per month, freemium with a 14-day trial. Estimated model cost ~$6 per user per month. Churned beta users indicate the personas still need refinement — the numbers here came from a founder interview, not a paying cohort.
